text: FADE IN:
EXT. SCOTT'S BACK YARD - NIGHT
A HOUSE BURNS. Flames breathe through smashed windows. An upstairs curtain lifts in the heat, then disappears.
SCOTT (late 20s) sits on the grass in his socks. His shirt is torn. One arm is blistered. He holds a phone against an ear that won't stop ringing.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: Sir? Stay with me. You said there were six people.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Yeah.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: How many got out?
Scott stares at the house. Somewhere inside, glass breaks.
He can't finish.
CUT TO:
INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - EARLIER
A hand scoops crisps from a bag into a bowl. Half miss. Scott picks them up, puts them in the bowl anyway.
The room is modest, tidy in the hurried way a room gets tidy before company. SIX glasses. SIX places at a dining table beyond the couch.
The doorbell. Scott brushes crumbs off his trousers and opens up.
DEENA (late 20s) walks straight in, followed by ANGELO (early 30s), who is carrying a six-pack and an unlit cigarette behind one ear.

speaker: DEENA
text: You moved the sofa.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Hi, Deena.

speaker: DEENA
text: I'm just saying. Last week you said it was too heavy to move.

speaker: ANGELO
text: You know who's coming tonight, right?
Scott takes the six-pack, gives Angelo a look.

speaker: SCOTT
text: You two can still go home.

speaker: DEENA
text: Aw. He missed us.
She kisses his cheek. Angelo tries to slip past with the cigarette.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Don't smoke in here.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I'm not smoking.

speaker: SCOTT
text: You've got one in your hair.
Angelo takes it down, discovers he has nowhere to put it, puts it back.

speaker: ANGELO
text: It's decorative.
A KNOCK. Scott reaches the front door a little too quickly.
KAY (late 20s) is on the step, holding a dripping bag of ice. Rain beads on her hair.

speaker: KAY
text: Before you tell me I didn't need to bring anything--

speaker: SCOTT
text: I wasn't going to.

speaker: KAY
text: You were. You did the face.
He steps back to let her in. Doesn't realize he's blocking the doorway until she nudges past.

speaker: SCOTT
text: It's just-- we've got ice.

speaker: KAY
text: Then I'm taking it home.

speaker: SCOTT
text: No, no. I'll take it.
She laughs, hands him the bag. A brief moment between them, almost a question. Neither asks it.

speaker: DEENA
text: Kay! Save yourself. He's rearranged the whole room.

speaker: KAY
text: Is that why it smells like furniture polish?

speaker: SCOTT
text: It does not.
Kay sniffs the air.

speaker: KAY
text: It really does.
She passes him. He smiles despite himself.
Another RING, followed at once by impatient KNOCKING.
CHRISTOF (late 20s) and MARINA (late 20s) wait on the porch, mid-argument.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Tell him what you told me.

speaker: MARINA
text: I said turn left at the second light.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: You said the light by the church.

speaker: MARINA
text: It's the same light.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: There are two churches.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Finally! You two coming in or what?

speaker: MARINA
text: See? Two people heard that address and only one got us lost.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: She's been rehearsing that in the car.
They come in, laughing over each other. Scott shuts the door.
The latch CLICKS. Then, just as his hand leaves it, another quiet CLICK.
He checks the lock. It is secure. He lets it go.
INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - LATER
Music. Glasses clink. Somebody's left wet footprints by the door. Everyone is talking at once and nobody minds.
Christof is telling a story with a biscuit in his hand.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: I thought it was a date. That's my point.

speaker: DEENA
text: You said she brought her brother.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: I'm getting to that.

speaker: KAY
text: Why didn't you leave?

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: I'd already bought a drink.

speaker: ANGELO
text: That's not a reason.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: It was a twelve-quid drink.
Marina wipes a wine ring off Scott's table. Scott notices, hands her a coaster without thinking.

speaker: MARINA
text: Thank you. The table's going to live.

speaker: SCOTT
text: It's a borrowed table.

speaker: MARINA
text: That explains the tension.
Kay leans against the kitchen doorway, watching Scott hover between cups and snacks.

speaker: KAY
text: Sit down, Scott.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I'm sitting.

speaker: KAY
text: You're standing.
Scott glances at his own legs. Sits on the arm of the couch.

speaker: KAY
text: Better.
Deena sees them. Almost comments. Decides not to.
Angelo pulls a deck of cards from its box.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Are we doing this, then? Or did we all come here to hear Christof say "exposure" again?

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: You liked that story.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I liked when it ended.
INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - DINING AREA - MOMENTS LATER
They gather at the table. The kind of rearranging that takes three conversations and twice as long as it should.
Deena swaps Angelo's glass with her own. He doesn't notice. Christof drags over the last chair for Marina.
Angelo shuffles. He flashes the cards. A poor magician pretending to be a professional.

speaker: DEENA
text: Just deal them.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Can I enjoy something?

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Not in this house, apparently.
The first cards fly. One pile. Another. Another.
Scott is telling Kay something under the noise of the table.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I was going to text you about Saturday.

speaker: KAY
text: You mean the text you started on Monday?

speaker: SCOTT
text: I didn't--

speaker: KAY
text: Deena told me.
Scott looks toward Deena. She concentrates very hard on her drink.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Right. Good.
Kay smiles. Doesn't rescue him.

speaker: KAY
text: What about Saturday?
Before he can answer--

speaker: DEENA
text: Angelo.
The cards stop.

speaker: ANGELO
text: What?

speaker: DEENA
text: Who's that for?
She points at a pile.
There are SEVEN HANDS on the table.
Angelo looks at the pile, then at the cards left in his hand.

speaker: ANGELO
text: That's mine.

speaker: DEENA
text: Then what's that?

speaker: ANGELO
text: ...Also mine, I guess.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Take both. You'll still lose.
A couple of laughs. Angelo laughs too, but keeps checking the piles.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Hold on. Did someone move one?

speaker: MARINA
text: No.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Just pick them up.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I am picking them up.
He gathers the cards. Shuffles. Deals again, slower this time.
One. Two. Three. Four. Five. SIX cards.
Each person at the table has a card. Angelo has the deck, and no card in front of him.
He looks at his empty place.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Right. Okay.

speaker: DEENA
text: What now?

speaker: ANGELO
text: How have I done it again?

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: You haven't. There are six.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Yeah. There's six. Where's mine?
Christof looks. He starts to answer, then stops.

speaker: MARINA
text: Did you deal yourself first?

speaker: ANGELO
text: No. I went around.

speaker: DEENA
text: You're making it into a whole thing.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Can you just-- everybody touch the card in front of you.

speaker: DEENA
text: Why?

speaker: ANGELO
text: Please.
Six hands come down on six cards. Angelo still holds the deck.
One beat. Two.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Maybe you don't get to play.
It's supposed to be funny. Nobody laughs as much as they ought to.

speaker: KAY
text: I'm going to the loo. This is making me stupid.
She stands, stepping around Scott's chair.

speaker: SCOTT
text: You want me to--

speaker: KAY
text: No. Save my seat, though.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I can manage that.

speaker: KAY
text: Big night for you.
She squeezes his shoulder as she goes. Scott watches her disappear down the corridor.
A bathroom door CLICKS somewhere out of sight.
Angelo scoops up the cards.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Okay. With Kay gone, five people. Yes?

speaker: DEENA
text: Please don't start.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Five. It's five.
He deals. Four around the table. The fifth to himself.
Perfect.

speaker: ANGELO
text: See?

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Well done. How old are you?

speaker: ANGELO
text: Go on. Laugh. I'm delighted for you.

speaker: DEENA
text: Can we play now?
Angelo stares at the fifth card, his smile slowly draining. He can't explain what just happened.
INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - DINING AREA - LATER
The game has become noisy again. Cards hit the table. Someone is halfway through a story nobody else believes.
Six piles now. Six people apparently playing. No one acknowledges when Kay came back. Her chair is tucked in, but she isn't visible in any clear, uninterrupted view.
Christof throws down his last card.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Thank you. I'll accept apologies individually.

speaker: DEENA
text: That was luck.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: Keep saying it. Makes it sweeter.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Champion's buying the next bottle.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: I brought the last one.

speaker: MARINA
text: You drank most of it.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: That's not evidence.

speaker: SCOTT
text: There's another in the kitchen. Left cupboard.
Christof gets up, eyes Angelo's hand.

speaker: CHRISTOF
text: And don't touch my cards.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Your cards are awful. Why would I?
Christof goes through to the kitchen.
Scott looks at Kay's glass. It still holds its first pour. A small red lip mark on the rim, but hardly any wine gone.
He taps the glass with a fingernail, considering it.
From the kitchen--
A short, choking GASP.
A METALLIC CRASH.
Everyone jolts. Scott starts up.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Christof?
No response.

speaker: MARINA
text: What was that?
Scott takes a step toward the kitchen.
A bottle of wine comes down onto the table behind him with a soft THUMP.

speaker: DEENA
text: Scott, you're standing on my foot.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Sorry.
He looks down, moves. When he looks up, the bottle is there. So are five fresh glasses. His concern dissolves into the simple habit of being the host.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Oh. Thanks.
No one answers. He uncorks the wine and pours.

speaker: DEENA
text: That's plenty.
He stops. He's overfilled her glass.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Sorry. Just tell me when.

speaker: DEENA
text: I did. Twice.
Scott looks again at Kay's untouched glass.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Where's Kay?

speaker: DEENA
text: Bathroom.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Still?

speaker: DEENA
text: I don't know. Go ask her.
Scott looks along the empty hallway. Bathroom door closed.

speaker: MARINA
text: Don't. She'll come out when she's ready.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I just thought she was here a second ago.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Maybe she was.
Scott looks at him. Angelo can't make the sentence mean anything sensible.

speaker: MARINA
text: We'll start when Christof gets back.

speaker: SCOTT
text: He did come back.
Marina glances towards the doorway.

speaker: MARINA
text: He went to get the wine.
Scott is holding the wine.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Yeah. This wine.
They all look at the bottle. Christof is nowhere in the room.

speaker: DEENA
text: Probably went for a smoke.

speaker: SCOTT
text: He doesn't smoke.

speaker: DEENA
text: Then I don't know, Scott.
Nobody admits how long they've been avoiding the kitchen door.
Angelo reaches for the deck.

speaker: ANGELO
text: We can do one quick hand. Until they come back.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Both of them?

speaker: ANGELO
text: Yeah. Kay and Christof.
Scott nods. It sounds right. Then it doesn't.
INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - DINING AREA - CONTINUOUS
The cards land. Angelo gets through four piles. Then a FIFTH.
Deena catches his wrist before he can deal again.

speaker: DEENA
text: Angelo. Stop.

speaker: ANGELO
text: What?

speaker: DEENA
text: Count those.
He does. Five.
He looks around the table. Scott. Deena. Marina. Himself.

speaker: ANGELO
text: No.

speaker: SCOTT
text: What?
Angelo shoves his chair back. A sharp scrape across the floor.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Is somebody messing with me?

speaker: DEENA
text: Nobody's touching the cards except you.

speaker: ANGELO
text: That's what I'm saying.

speaker: MARINA
text: Angelo, sit down.

speaker: ANGELO
text: No, hang on. Just-- hands. Give me your hands.

speaker: SCOTT
text: What are you doing?

speaker: ANGELO
text: I want to count the people. Not the cards. Just give me your hand, Scott.

speaker: DEENA
text: You're actually scaring me now.
That lands. Angelo looks at her, softens.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I'm not trying to. Come on. It'll take ten seconds.
Reluctantly they link hands around the table. Four people. In Scott's left hand is Marina's warm, ringed hand. In his right, a hand he takes for Angelo's.

speaker: ANGELO
text: All right. Just say who's on your left. Don't let go. Somebody start.
A perfectly familiar voice, from somewhere around the table:

speaker: VOICE
text: Scott.
Scott doesn't react. He looks left.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Marina.

speaker: MARINA
text: Deena.

speaker: DEENA
text: Angelo.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Scott.
The names hang in the room.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Wait.

speaker: DEENA
text: What?

speaker: SCOTT
text: Didn't somebody already say me?

speaker: ANGELO
text: I just did.

speaker: SCOTT
text: No. Before that.

speaker: MARINA
text: Yeah. I heard it.
Angelo looks at each of them. His grip tightens.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Okay. Other way. Right this time.

speaker: DEENA
text: Angelo--

speaker: ANGELO
text: Just do it.
Scott looks to his right.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Angelo.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Deena.

speaker: DEENA
text: Marina.

speaker: MARINA
text: Scott.
Scott looks from one face to the next. Then down at their hands. He can't make the circle fit.
Someone at the table says, very softly--

speaker: VOICE
text: Angelo.
No one moves.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Who said that?
No answer. The ordinary hum of the refrigerator suddenly feels loud.

speaker: DEENA
text: Scott, whose hand have you got?
Scott looks down. He is holding Angelo's hand. Of course he is.
But there is a FIFTH wineglass between them, set on a coaster.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Why's that there?

speaker: ANGELO
text: Don't let go yet.
Marina lets go anyway. They all break contact at once.

speaker: MARINA
text: Okay, that's enough. Somebody take a photo.

speaker: DEENA
text: Of what?

speaker: MARINA
text: Us. All of us. Right now.
She pulls out her phone, hands it to someone without ever quite looking at who takes it.

speaker: MARINA
text: Just get everyone in.
A moment of awkward shuffling. Scott, Deena, Angelo and Marina stand together against the wall. Marina's hand trembles on Scott's shoulder.
A CAMERA SHUTTER.
And the phone is back in Marina's hand.
They crowd around the screen. Four people in the photograph. None of them is holding the phone.

speaker: DEENA
text: Four. There's four of us.

speaker: MARINA
text: I can see that.
Angelo zooms in. The image is sharp. The photographer stood several feet away.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Who took it?

speaker: MARINA
text: Christof.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Kay.
Both answer at once. Then both look towards the empty hall.

speaker: MARINA
text: No. I gave it to--
She stops. Looks at her own hand as if it might tell her.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Kay's in the bathroom.

speaker: ANGELO
text: And Christof's in the kitchen.
He doesn't raise his voice. That is somehow worse.

speaker: DEENA
text: Then let's go get them.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Together.
No one argues.
INT. SCOTT'S HOUSE - HALLWAY / KITCHEN - CONTINUOUS
Four people make a slow, uncomfortable procession past the closed bathroom door.
Scott puts his hand toward its handle. Stops. He has no idea why.

speaker: MARINA
text: Scott?

speaker: SCOTT
text: Yeah. Coming.
They enter the kitchen.
Empty. A cupboard door stands open. One chair has been pushed away from the little breakfast counter.

speaker: DEENA
text: Christof?
Nothing.
A quiet HISS threads through the silence.
Marina covers her nose.

speaker: MARINA
text: What's that smell?
Scott's eyes go to the stove. Two burner knobs are missing. Broken plastic lies half-hidden under the cabinet.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Oh, shit. Gas.

speaker: DEENA
text: Turn it off.

speaker: SCOTT
text: The knobs are gone.

speaker: MARINA
text: So turn it off behind the stove.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I'm trying.
He grips the appliance. It barely budges. He pulls harder. Something heavy shifts inside with a damp, ugly sound.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Leave it. We'll get outside and call someone.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Just one second.
His hand finds the oven handle. Deena takes one step toward him.

speaker: DEENA
text: Scott, don't--
He opens it.
CHRISTOF is folded inside the oven. His head is crushed against the back wall. Blood has pooled beneath his bent limbs.
Scott makes a small sound, not even a scream at first. His legs give way. Then the screaming starts.

speaker: MARINA
text: Oh, God. Oh, God--

speaker: ANGELO
text: No. No, no--
Deena grabs Scott by the shoulders to pull him back. Scott turns toward her.
For an instant, she's fine.
Then her throat OPENS.
No knife. No figure. A terrible line appears across her neck and becomes a wound.
Deena clamps her palms over it. Her eyes fix on Angelo, disbelieving. Something behind her JERKS her head upright as she tries to fall.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Dee?
He moves to her, almost slips in the blood, catches her before she hits the tiles.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Hey. Hey, look at me. Look at me.
Deena tries to breathe. A wet, desperate flutter. Her fingers lose their strength.

speaker: ANGELO
text: No, no. Stay. Come on, Dee. Come on.
Her body goes quiet. Angelo holds her anyway.
Scott backs into the counter, grabs a kitchen knife. His hand won't stop shaking.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Where is it?
Angelo looks up.

speaker: ANGELO
text: What?

speaker: SCOTT
text: There was-- something had her. I saw her hair--

speaker: ANGELO
text: I didn't see anybody.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I know.
He scans the kitchen, knife out, breathing hard.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Marina? Marina, get away from the door.
No answer. Marina is gone.
Scott looks to the hall. Empty.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Marina?
He takes a step. Stops. He can't bear to put his back to Angelo.

speaker: SCOTT
text: She was here. She was just here.
Angelo is staring at the patch of floor beside Deena. There is blood there, pressed into the shape of a hand. No hand remains.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I was holding her.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I know.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I was right there.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Angelo, we need to go.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Then how did it--
He looks at the bloody floor again. Breaks off.

speaker: SCOTT
text: We go out the back. Now. Come on.
Angelo gently lays Deena down. Takes his jacket off and covers her throat, far too late.

speaker: ANGELO
text: When you counted us. You kept saying five.

speaker: SCOTT
text: What?

speaker: ANGELO
text: The cards. The picture. I thought I was--
He tries again. Can't.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Don't. Don't think about that. We get outside.

speaker: ANGELO
text: And whoever did this just comes with us?
Scott glances over his shoulder toward the empty hallway. He has no answer.
The HISS grows louder. Or perhaps they are finally listening.

speaker: SCOTT
text: The gas. Angelo, we have to shut the gas off.
Angelo looks at the stove. Then at Deena.
He takes the forgotten cigarette from behind his ear. Stares at it, then drops it to the floor.
He reaches into his pocket and takes out a cheap metal LIGHTER.
Scott sees it.

speaker: SCOTT
text: No.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Back door's there.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Put it down.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Go, Scott.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Just-- think for one second.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I have.
Scott edges toward him. Angelo takes a step back.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Come with me. We can call the police from outside.

speaker: ANGELO
text: And say what?
A beat. Scott glances down at Deena and away again.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I don't know.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Neither do I.
The kitchen is silent except for the gas.

speaker: ANGELO
text: You always keep the back gate unlocked?

speaker: SCOTT
text: Yeah.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Good. Go through it. Don't stop in the yard.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Angelo--

speaker: ANGELO
text: Scott. Please.
It is the first time all night he hasn't sounded like himself.
Scott cannot move.

speaker: ANGELO
text: I don't want you here when I do it.
He raises the lighter. His thumb trembles against the wheel.

speaker: SCOTT
text: You don't have to--

speaker: ANGELO
text: Go.
A long beat. Angelo looks once more at Deena.

speaker: ANGELO
text: Sorry about your house.
His thumb strikes. A SPARK that fails to catch.
Scott runs.
EXT. SCOTT'S BACK YARD - CONTINUOUS
He flies through the door, nearly falls down the steps, grabs the handle to pull it shut.
From inside: the tiny, dry SCRAPE of a lighter wheel.
The kitchen ERUPTS.
The blast throws Scott down the steps. Windows burst outward. Heat washes the grass. His shirt catches; he rolls, scrambles, rolls again until the fire dies.
He crawls to the far fence, coughing and sobbing. A second explosion sends sparks into the night.
For a while, there is nothing he can do but watch.
EXT. SCOTT'S BACK YARD - LATER
Flames eat through the upstairs rooms. Red lights strobe faintly through the fence from the street beyond.
Scott has found his phone. His thumb shakes so badly he misses the emergency number twice.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: Emergency services. What is your address?
Scott gives it, barely getting the words out. She asks him to stay on the line.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: Are you injured?

speaker: SCOTT
text: Yeah. I-- yeah.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: Help is coming. Is anybody still inside?
Scott looks at the house. A window collapses inward.

speaker: SCOTT
text: My friends.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: How many friends?

speaker: SCOTT
text: Five. I had five over.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: And are they all still inside?
He tries to count. Deena. Christof. Angelo. Kay. Marina. He can't make the numbers stay still in his head.

speaker: SCOTT
text: I don't know. I don't know where-- I don't know.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: Sir, listen to me. You're outside. You're safe for now.
He hears her but doesn't believe her.

speaker: DISPATCHER
text: How many people made it out?
Scott wipes his face on his sleeve.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Me.
A pause. He feels something warm close around his free hand.
He doesn't look down. He just squeezes back. Relief, so sudden it hurts.

speaker: SCOTT
text: Two.
He lowers the phone a little. On the grass beside him: THEIR HANDS, held tight.
No second figure is visible.
The house burns. The two hands do not separate.
FADE OUT.
THE END
